title: Looking at an already-submitted notification, the frontend still shows 'Now submit your notification' and a Continue button that leads nowhere; DR1 hides the submit form once the notification has been submitted.

finding.frontend: A user who opens a notification they have already submitted, through the View link on the dashboard, reads 'Check your answers' under a green Submitted tag, scrolls past every answer with no way to change any of them — and arrives at a heading saying 'Now submit your notification', a sentence saying 'Continue to the declaration to submit your notification.' and a live Continue button. fe-check-answers-submitted is that page. The read-only treatment is working everywhere else on it: the controller sets readOnly when the journey status is SUBMITTED (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/controller.js:81) and not one Change link is rendered. The submit block at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:108-114 simply sits outside every readOnly test, so the one thing the page still offers is the one thing the user has already done. Pressing Continue goes to the declaration, which bounces straight to the confirmation page for a notification they did not just submit.
finding.prototype: The review page renders the same cards read-only for a submitted notification, and wraps the whole submit form in a readOnly test so neither the form nor the Continue button appears (app/views/review-notification.html:181-187, reached with readOnly true from app/routes.js:10024-10037). A submitted notification is presented as a record, with no action on it.
finding.difference: Wrap the submit heading, the explanatory sentence and the Continue form in the existing readOnly condition on the check-answers template, so a submitted notification shows no submit action. The readOnly flag is already computed and already used on the same page for the Change links, so nothing new has to be worked out.
finding.falsifiedBy: Opening the frontend's Check your answers page for a submitted notification and finding no Continue button on it.
finding.correction:
Stands, and the medium confidence is honestly earned — the finding says in its own words that the captured frontend page is a draft and that this state is not in the corpus, so it reads as a statement of the rules rather than of an observation. Every limb re-checked in source. readOnly is set from the journey status at check-answers/controller.js:81. It suppresses the Change links through editableActions at check-answers/view-model/rows/change-link.js:28, which returns an empty object when readOnly. The submit block at check-answers/template.njk:108-114 sits at the top level of the content block, after every card loop has closed, with no readOnly test anywhere above it — so it renders whatever the status. The onward claim is verified too: declaration/controller.js:49-54 redirects a SUBMITTED journey straight to the confirmation page on GET, so Continue lands the user on a confirmation for a notification they did not just submit. DR1's counterpart is the `{% if not readOnly %}` at app/views/review-notification.html:181-187, and the citation is exact. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: fe-check-answers-submitted was shot after this finding was written, reaching the page the way a user does — the View link on the dashboard for a submitted notification — and it shows everything the finding claimed. Confidence raised from medium to high. The page carries a green 'Submitted' tag, and the submit block below the last card is intact: `

Now submit your notification

`, the paragraph 'Continue to the declaration to submit your notification.' and a `
` with a live Continue button. Two things the picture adds to the argument. The finding named only the Continue button; the heading and the sentence render too, so the page tells the user in three ways to do something already done — the fix is the whole block, as `difference` says, not just the button. And the readOnly flag is demonstrably live on the same page: the captured DOM holds no Change link anywhere, where the draft capture of the same page holds twenty-eight. So this is not a flag that failed to compute, it is a block that was never put inside it, which is why the fix is as small as `difference` says.

relatedTo.why: both change the block of content below the last card
